edition.locus: De Creatis (Photius Bibl. 235 / TLG 2959.005) §2 faith reductio

source_text: ἢ οὖν πᾶσι τοῖς Ἕλλησι καὶ τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀπίστοις ταῦτα παρεβλήθη παρὰ τῶν τοῦ Χριστοῦ μαθητῶν καὶ ἐκηρύχθη, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀσεβείας μετέβαλεν αὐτοὺς εἰς τὴν εἰς Χριστὸν πίστιν ὥσπερ οὖν καὶ πιστεύοντες ὁμολογοῦμεν, καὶ οὐκέτι δύναται νοεῖσθαι τό »μὴ βάλητε τοὺς μαργαρίτας ὑμῶν ἔμπροσθεν τῶν χοίρων«, ὡς ἐρρήθη· ἢ τούτου ὡς ἐλέχθη νοουμένου, ἀνάγκη ἡμᾶς λέγειν ὡς οὐδενὶ τῶν ἀπίστων, οὓς ἀπεικάζομεν, ἐκ τῶν ἀποστολικῶν διδαγμάτων, μαργαριτῶν δίκην τὰς ψυχὰς καταυγαζόντων, ἡ εἰς Χριστὸν πίστις καὶ ἡ τῆς ἀσεβείας ἐλευθερία γεγένηται. βλάσφημον δὲ τοῦτο.
pass_a_gloss: or therefore to-all the Greeks and the other unbelievers these-things were-cast-before by the of-the Christ disciples and were-proclaimed, and from the impiety it-changed them into the into Christ faith just-as therefore also believing we-confess, and no-longer is-able to-be-understood the “do-not throw the pearls of-you before the pigs,” as was-said; or of-this as was-said being-understood, necessity us to-say that to-none of-the unbelievers, whom we-were-likening, from the apostolic teachings, of-pearls like the souls illuminating, the into Christ faith and the of-the impiety freedom has-come-about. blasphemous and this.
pass_b_english: Either these things were set before all the Greeks and the other unbelievers by Christ’s disciples and were proclaimed, and turned them from impiety to faith in Christ — just as we who believe confess — and then “do not throw your pearls before pigs” can no longer be read as it was said;

or, if that saying is taken as it was said, we are forced to claim that faith in Christ and freedom from impiety never came to any of the unbelievers we were comparing — from the apostolic teachings that light the soul like pearls. And that is blasphemous.

choices.why: Double εἰς kept as faith directed to Christ, not vague ‘Christian belief’.
Genitive of separation; liberation from ungodliness, not abstract free will.
Public apostolic preaching to outsiders — universal-call hinge of the reductio.
